fields.description:
Stop `rebar init` from silently creating an empty divergent store when it cannot obtain the configured tickets branch. This fixes P1 `01e8-302b`.

## Current mechanism

`_mount_or_create_branch` currently checks only local refs and the local remote-tracking ref. If both are absent, it immediately creates an orphan branch. A failed or timed-out fetch can therefore make an existing remote branch look like a genuine first init. `pending_init_attaches_to_existing` repeats the same ref-only predicate. Both `ensure_store_mounted_best_effort` and `_create_tracker` in `src/rebar/_cli/_init.py` consume that predicate, so every path must share one tri-state result and distinguish unreachable from genuinely absent.

The current code already bounds the cold materializing fetch with `_git_fetch` and `_FETCH_TIMEOUT = 300`. Preserve that behavior. Add a shorter bounded remote-advertisement probe through a shared network runner rather than duplicating the timeout wrapper. Use `git ls-remote --exit-code <remote> refs/heads/<branch>`: return code 0 means advertised, 2 means reachable but absent, and timeout or another failure means unreachable.

## Implementation plan

- Generalize the existing bounded Git-network seam so `_git_fetch` retains its 300-second cold-fetch contract and a new advertisement probe uses a short named timeout. Both convert `TimeoutExpired` to a descriptive `CompletedProcess(124)`.
- Add one shared tri-state remote-branch probe consumed by `_mount_or_create_branch`, `pending_init_attaches_to_existing`, `ensure_store_mounted_best_effort`, and `_create_tracker` whenever neither a local branch nor a local remote-tracking ref exists.
- Cache only the tri-state probe result for a short named TTL, keyed by resolved repo, remote, and branch. The first best-effort-mount probe and immediately following strict auto-init reuse one result, so an unreachable remote costs at most one probe timeout per CLI invocation. Inject the monotonic clock for a test that advances past the TTL and proves later calls re-probe.
- Preserve `ensure_store_mounted_best_effort` as a non-raising best-effort API. It treats unreachable as do-not-auto-mount and returns without error. Its `init_core` call continues to use `force_new_store=False`, supplied by the default or explicitly, and it never authorizes an override.
- Update `_create_tracker` to distinguish reachable-absent from unreachable. Unreachable fails closed with the remote diagnostic and never enters the interactive consent gate. The preceding best-effort path and strict path reuse the cached result.
- If the remote advertises the branch, attempt the existing bounded fetch. Mount only after the branch materializes. If fetch fails, return nonzero with an error naming the configured remote and branch plus fetch-and-retry remediation. Never create an orphan in this state.
- If the remote is reachable and does not advertise the branch, preserve legitimate first-init orphan bootstrap.
- If the probe cannot reach the remote or times out, fail closed with a distinct error naming the remote, branch, timeout where applicable, retry remediation, and explicit deliberate-bootstrap override. Never create an orphan unless the override was supplied.
- Add `--force-new-store` to explicit CLI init, thread `force_new_store=False` through `init_core`, and expose the equivalent keyword on `rebar.init_repo`. Auto-init and `ensure_store_mounted_best_effort` never supply the override; only an explicit CLI flag or library keyword can authorize bootstrap while reachability is unknown.
- The override applies only to unreachable. When the remote is reachable, warn that `--force-new-store` has no effect and continue normal behavior: reachable-absent bootstraps normally; advertised fetches and mounts or fails nonzero without orphaning.
- Update `src/rebar/_cli/help/init.txt` and regenerate `docs/cli-reference.md` for the new flag.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a reachable remote advertising the configured tickets branch but no local remote-tracking ref, a simulated bounded fetch failure returns nonzero and creates no orphan branch. Tier: CLI subprocess with real temporary repositories.
- [ ] With a reachable remote that does not advertise the configured branch, init still bootstraps successfully. Tier: CLI subprocess negative control.
- [ ] With an unreachable or timing-out remote, explicit init and strict auto-init return nonzero within one probe bound, create no orphan branch, and emit an error distinct from advertised/fetch-failed. Strict auto-init does not enter the consent prompt. Proving command: `pytest tests/integration/test_init_fail_closed.py -k unreachable -v`.
- [ ] `ensure_store_mounted_best_effort` treats unreachable as do-not-auto-mount, returns without error, and never supplies `force_new_store=True`; the following strict path reuses the cached result and reports the actionable failure.
- [ ] `rebar init --force-new-store` and `rebar.init_repo(force_new_store=True)` permit deliberate bootstrap only when reachability cannot be established. Tier: CLI subprocess plus library interface test.
- [ ] With a reachable advertised branch, `--force-new-store` is ineffective: the command warns, attempts normal bounded fetch, and returns nonzero without an orphan if fetch fails. With reachable-absent, it warns and follows normal successful bootstrap. Tier: CLI subprocess negative controls.
- [ ] Failure messages name the configured remote, configured branch, timeout where applicable, and concrete fetch/retry or force-new-store remediation. Tier: unit assertions on stderr.
- [ ] An existing healthy store remains idempotent, does not invoke the advertisement probe, and is unaffected by the override default. Proving command: `pytest tests/integration/test_init_fail_closed.py -k idempotent -v`.
- [ ] `pending_init_attaches_to_existing` returns true when the remote advertises the branch despite no local remote-tracking ref, and false for reachable-absent and unreachable. Proving command: `pytest tests/unit/test_init_attach_predicate.py -v`.
- [ ] Behavioral wiring tests monkeypatch the one shared probe and prove `_mount_or_create_branch`, `pending_init_attaches_to_existing`, `ensure_store_mounted_best_effort`, and `_create_tracker` consume it; a second independent remote-existence predicate fails the tests.
- [ ] One CLI invocation performs at most one underlying advertisement probe on the unreachable path; advancing the injected monotonic clock past the short TTL causes a fresh probe. Tier: unit orchestration test.
- [ ] Existing timeout tests continue proving cold fetch retains its 300-second bound, while new tests prove the advertisement probe has its own positive short bound and folds timeout to return code 124.
- [ ] `rebar init --help` and generated `docs/cli-reference.md` both contain `--force-new-store` and its deliberate-bootstrap semantics. Proving commands: `rebar init --help | grep -- --force-new-store` and `grep -- --force-new-store docs/cli-reference.md`.

## Files

Production and docs: `src/rebar/_commands/init.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_init.py`, `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/help/init.txt`, and generated `docs/cli-reference.md`.

Tests: new `tests/integration/test_init_fail_closed.py` and `tests/unit/test_init_attach_predicate.py`; update existing direct-call and timeout coverage including `tests/unit/test_git_timeout_bounds_983f.py` and `tests/unit/test_sync_remote_config.py`, plus other directly affected init CLI/library tests discovered during the RED-first inventory.

Scope: S-M. No dependencies.
